signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/CHF trades at 0.5810, holding above its SMA20 at 0.5780 while the overall trend structure shows short-term evidence turning against the broader downtrend. In G10 weekly performance, AUD leads as the top performer at +0.544% across 4 pairs while CHF lags as the weakest at -0.713% across 6 pairs, driving a 1.257% leader-to-laggard spread. A 460bp CB rate differential (RBA 4.60% vs SNB 0.00%) strongly favors AUD carry, further reinforced by an OIS carry advantage. With VIX at 18.4 (normal volatility), risk sentiment remains contained enough to let carry differentials drive cross performance over low-yielding safe havens. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; massive carry premium and broad G10 divergence support the pair. Catalyst: Australia Q3 CPI release on 28 Oct (forecast 4.7% y/y). Risk: Australia CPI misses expectations, dampening RBA hawkish sentiment and triggering a squeeze in long positioning.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY sits at 157.432, trading below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 157.87, SMA50 at 157.55) in a firm downtrend following recent sharp downside momentum. Fed at 4.00% vs BoJ at 1.25% provides a +275bp policy rate differential (+267bp on OIS SOFR/TONA basis) favoring USD, but options markets show acute downside hedging with 25d Risk Reversals printing a strong put skew at -2.15. CFTC positioning shows JPY Leveraged Funds net short at -25,598 (pctl 94, z +1.43), indicating spec positioning remains historically elevated on the short side despite recent WoW short covering (+12,222 contracts). Divergence between a heavy spec JPY short and aggressive downside options skew highlights elevated crash-protection buying ahead of upcoming central bank decisions. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; severe negative options skew and technical weakness cap upside despite carry advantage. Catalyst: Fed interest rate decision on 28 Oct followed by BoJ CPI release and rate decision. Risk: Fed delivers a hawkish stance while BoJ remains dovish, reigniting carry demand and pushing spot above 158.50.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Options VRP + Technical Resistance
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1188, positioned below its SMA20 (1.1238), SMA50 (1.1440), and SMA200 (1.1579) in an established downtrend. Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% establishes a 135bp policy rate differential (+146bp OIS basis) supporting USD, while COT Leveraged Funds remain heavily short EUR at net -94,138 contracts (pctl 2, z -1.72), reflecting extreme negative speculative sentiment. Options market pricing reflects significant hedging demand with 1M ATM IV at 6.5% vs HV30 at 4.1%, generating an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.4%. EUR/USD is also notably cheap on BEER fair value models at z = -2.62σ (spot 1.1188 vs model 1.1317), suggesting downside momentum is stretched relative to macro fundamentals. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; strong structural rate spread and intact downtrend keep pair under pressure despite extreme spec shorts. Catalyst: ECB interest rate decision on 29 Oct. Risk: Hawkish ECB surprise triggers a sharp short-squeeze out of lower-decile spec positioning toward 1.1300.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.316, positioned below its SMA20 (9.503), SMA50 (9.411), and SMA200 (9.518) in a clear technical downtrend. Norges Bank at 4.50% vs Fed at 4.00% creates a 50bp carry differential supporting NOK, matching Norway's positive ESI of +14.0 which signals persistent economic data beats. Retail sentiment exhibits a 100% extreme long allocation on USD/NOK, establishing an extreme one-sided crowd attempting to bottom-fish against the prevailing trend. Meanwhile, US 5Y real yields declined 25bp over 5D (FRED, as of Oct 22), removing structural yield support from the dollar. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to retail extreme and aligned with negative rate spreads. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy decision on 5 Nov. Risk: Sharp rebound in WTI crude oil prices dropping below $95/bbl that weakens NOK back above SMA20 resistance at 9.50.
